[GEPA](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.19457) evolves **module prompts**, not weights. A reflection LM distills lessons from its own system’s execution trajectories and evaluator feedback, overlapping trajectory distillation, teacher guidance, and fixed-model adaptation—not necessarily teacher–student training (§3, lines 00270–00283).

Reflection attributes successes and failures to prompt elements; it does not specify cross-trajectory program-state matching. Some generated instructions align summaries with downstream retrieval needs (§3, lines 00280–00281; Appendix L.1, lines 01683–01699). Merge combines non-ancestor lineages sharing an ancestor, using module-prompt differences, not independent trajectories or semantic-state alignment (Appendix D.1, lines 01184–01190, 01216–01236).

Candidates must improve minibatch scores; instance-wise Pareto sampling guides evolution, and validation average selects the final prompt. This overlaps skill verification, but verifies system performance rather than standalone skills (§3, lines 00212–00234; §3.1, lines 00288–00289).

The authors report cross-model transfer, but merge sometimes degraded performance and validation consumed most rollouts (§4, lines 00457–00459, 00510–00512). We did not replicate these claims. GEPA does not test our functional-state-aligned versus chronological extraction comparison under fixed evidence and budgets.
